# The field and multiplicative group generated by Mahler measures of conjugate monomials and their radicals

<a id="statement"></a>
## The field, its units and the number of distinct measures

Let \(w\) be a nontorsion algebraic unit at a chosen complex embedding.
Write \(V\) for the rational span of the multiplicative classes of its conjugates modulo roots of unity, written additively, and \(D(w)\) for the inverse image of \(V\) in the algebraic numbers of nonzero modulus.
Thus elements of \(D(w)\) are torsion twists of radicals of ordinary conjugate monomials.
Let \(L\) be the fixed field of the kernel of the absolute Galois action on \(V\), \(G=\operatorname{Gal}(L/\mathbb Q)\), \(c\) ordinary complex conjugation in this action, and \(r=\dim V^c\).
Use the linear functional \(\ell([x])=\log|x|\), extended to \(V_{\mathbb R}\).
Let
\[
 H=\{g\in G:\ell\circ g=\ell\},\qquad F=L^H,\qquad
 U=\{a\in D(w)\cap F:a>0\}.
\]
The positivity is at the given embedding.
Write \(\mathcal M\) for the multiplicative group generated by the actual numbers \(M(x)\) for \(x\in D(w)\), and put \(\nu=2\) if some \(g\in G\) carries \(\ell\) to \(-\ell\), and \(\nu=1\) otherwise.
Then
\[
 U^{\nu|H|}\subseteq\mathcal M\subseteq U,\qquad
 \operatorname{rank}\mathcal M=r,\qquad
 \mathbb Q\bigl(M(x):x\in D(w)\bigr)=F.                                  \tag{1}
\]
In particular all the measure values lie in one specified real embedded field, and they generate a group of finite index in its positive \(D(w)\)-units.
The bound in (1) is on the exponent of the quotient, rather than on its order.

The finitely many hyperplanes \(\ker(\ell\circ g)\) cut \(V_{\mathbb R}\) into open chambers.
For each chamber \(C\), let \(A_C=\sum_{\ell(gv)>0}g\) with \(v\in C\), and put \(s=\max_C\operatorname{rank} A_C\).
The rank uses the rational representation \(V\).
For the set of distinct real number values one has, as \(T\to\infty\),
\[
 \#\{M(x):x\in D(w),\ \log M(x)\le T\}\asymp_w (1+T)^s,\qquad
                \lceil r/2\rceil\le s\le r.                              \tag{2}
\]
Ordinary monomials in the conjugates already attain the lower growth order.
For a totally real cubic example below \(r=2\) and \(s=1\).
The constants in the counting estimate can vary with the generating unit.

<a id="field"></a>
## Why the field contains the actual exterior products

The splitting field of \(w\) is finite and its action supplies the quotient defining \(L\).
If \(m\) is the order of its group of roots of unity, all the \(m\)-th powers of the original conjugates belong to \(L\).
Indeed an automorphism acting trivially on classes sends each conjugate to a torsion multiple in that splitting field.
Consequently ordinary products of these powers in \(L\) give a full lattice of classes spanning \(V\).
The [fixed-space description of radial rank](Yin_C_G0901_v62.md#modules) gives \(r\ge1\).
More explicitly \(\ell\) vanishes on \(V^{-c}\) and is injective on the rational subspace \(V^c\).
If a fixed rational class has log modulus zero, take a representative \(a\) with \([a]=[c(a)]\); then \([a c(a)]=2[a]\) and \(a c(a)=1\), so the class vanishes.
This also proves the injectivity using cleared denominators.

Use a rational positive definite \(G\)-invariant inner product.
For \(P=(1+c)/2\), the equality \(\ell(gv)=\ell(v)\) on rational \(v\) is equivalent by injectivity to \(P g=P\).
Taking adjoints shows this is equivalent to \(g\) fixing \(V^c\) pointwise.
Likewise \(\ell\circ g=-\ell\) is equivalent to \(g\) negating \(V^c\) pointwise.
Since \(c\in H\), it follows that \(V^H=V^c\) and \(F\) is real at the chosen embedding.
For \(x\in D(w)\), every lift of an element of \(H\) preserves the modulus of every conjugate of \(x\), including those differing by torsion.
It therefore permutes the exterior conjugates, whose product times a rational sign equals \(M(x)\).
This proves \(M(x)\in U\), including when the conjugates of \(x\) themselves lie outside \(L\).
Conversely the classes of \(U\) span \(V^H\): average the full lattice of classes from \(L\) over \(H\), using actual orbit products in \(F\) and squaring to assure positivity.
Since \(U\) is a subgroup of the units of one number field and has no nontrivial torsion, it is free abelian of rank \(r\).

<a id="crossing"></a>
## Products of four measure values recover powers of the units

If \(v=[x]\), its actual conjugates give
\[
       [M(x)]=\frac{\deg x}{|G|}\, A_C v                                  \tag{3}
\]
when \(v\) is in a chamber \(C\).
This follows by averaging the exterior product over a common finite normal closure: each actual embedding occurs equally often, and the condition that a root is exterior depends only on its class.
In particular \(A_C\) takes rational values and its image lies in \(V^H\), since left multiplication by \(H\) permutes the selected terms.

Choose chambers on opposite sides of \(\ker\ell\) at a point of no other distinct hyperplane.
Such a point exists in the hyperplane, including in dimension one where there is only one distinct hyperplane.
The only terms changing sign correspond to \(g\) satisfying \(\ell\circ g=\pm\ell\): proportionality with any other real scalar is excluded by a \(G\)-invariant norm on the dual space.
Denote the two chambers, in order of positive and negative value of \(\ell\), by \(C_+\) and \(C_-\).
Then \(A_{C_+}-A_{C_-}\) is the sum over \(H\) minus the sum over the possible negative coset.
On \(V^c\) this acts as \(\nu|H|\) times the identity.

Fix \(a\in U\).
In each of the two chambers choose a class \(p_\pm\) in the full lattice of ordinary conjugate products lying in \(L\), off the fixed spaces of all nonidentity elements of \(G\).
The group is faithful, so these are finitely many proper subspaces and the choice is possible by scaling rational points.
For a large integer \(k\), both \(kp_\pm\) and \(kp_\pm+[a]\) are regular classes in their respective chambers with trivial stabilizer.
Take actual representatives \(y_\pm\in L\) of \(kp_\pm\) from the ordinary products.
Then both \(y_\pm\) and \(a y_\pm\) generate \(L\), since their classes have trivial stabilizer.
Formula (3) with \(\deg x=|G|\) and positivity in the given real embedding give the identity of numbers
\[
             \frac{M(a y_+)M(y_-)}{M(y_+)M(a y_-)}=a^{\nu|H|}.
\]
Indeed their classes agree by the chamber difference, and two positive real numbers differing by a root of unity are equal.
This proves the group inclusions in (1).
The subgroup of \(G\) fixing all \(M(x)\) now fixes the whole rational span \(V^c\) of \(U\) pointwise, and hence lies in \(H\).
The field assertion of (1) follows by finite Galois correspondence.
The chamber difference has rank at least \(r\), while each summand has image in \(V^c\); this proves the rank inequalities in (2).

<a id="count"></a>
## Counting values including arguments on the chamber walls

For a class on a wall, use the map \(A_v=\sum_{\ell(gv)>0}g\) with exactly the strict inequalities.
If \(v\) is rational, (3) with this sum follows from the same embedding count.
On the rational subspace \(E\) spanned by all rational points in the relative interior of that face, the values of \(A_v\) lie in the image of \(A_v|_E\).
To compare with \(s\), perturb the face slightly in two opposite generic directions, obtaining chamber maps \(A_1,A_2\).
Each term with \(\ell(gv)=0\) on the face belongs to one of the two added sets.
For a rational point \(p\) of the face, \(\ell(gp)=0\) implies \(cgp=-gp\) by the rational injectivity used above.
For each chamber map, the added set is stable under \(g\mapsto cg\) since \(\ell\circ c=\ell\).
Its total action on \(p\) therefore vanishes, with an unpaired fixed term possible only when \(c=1\), in which case \(gp=0\).
Thus either adjacent generic chamber map agrees with \(A_v\) on \(E\).
All output classes, including on faces, lie in the finite union of the rational subspaces \(\operatorname{im} A_C\) of dimension at most \(s\).

The ordinary absolute logarithmic height satisfies \(h(M(x))\le (\deg x)h(x)=\log M(x)\), by summing heights of the exterior conjugates of a unit.
On \(U\) the height is a norm on its real lattice span, by the archimedean unit logarithm embedding in \(F\).
There are \(O_w((1+T)^s)\) lattice points of height at most \(T\) in the union of these finitely many rational subspaces.
The map from positive real values to their classes is injective, giving the upper bound.

For the lower bound take a chamber of rank \(s\).
Choose \(s\) vectors of the full ordinary product lattice in \(L\) whose images are linearly independent.
Choose another lattice vector \(p\) well inside the chamber off all nontrivial stabilizers.
By taking a fixed large positive multiple of \(p\), every point of its translate of the closed unit parallelepiped spanned by the chosen vectors lies in the chamber and off those same fixed spaces.
Dilate that translated parallelepiped by a positive integer \(k\) and take the \((k+1)^s\) grid points from coefficients \(0,\dots,k\).
They are actual ordinary monomials in \(L\) of degree \(|G|\), since their classes have trivial stabilizer.
Their heights, and thus their log measures, are \(O_w(k)\) by subadditivity and homogeneity on the fixed finite list of monomials.
Formula (3) takes distinct values on the grid since the selected images are independent.
This proves (2).

<a id="cubic"></a>
## Linear growth of the spectrum despite two independent radial directions

Take \(w\) to be a root of \(X^3-4X+1\).
The rational root test and its positive nonsquare discriminant \(229\) give a totally real splitting field with group \(S_3\).
The product of the three roots is \(-1\).
Their classes therefore span a quotient of the ordinary two-dimensional sum-zero representation of \(S_3\).
It is nonzero since the roots are nontorsion, so irreducibility makes this quotient the whole plane.
Here \(c=1\) and \(r=2\).
Identify the plane over the reals with \(\mathbb C\), with the three rotations acting by \(z\mapsto \zeta^j z\) and the three reflections by \(z\mapsto \zeta^j\bar z\), where \(\zeta=\exp(2\pi i/3)\).
For a generic \(v\), one or two rotations are selected by the strict positive sign because the three vectors sum to zero.
The same count of one or two applies separately to the reflections.
The sum of either one or two distinct cube roots of unity has absolute value one.
Thus \(A_C z=a z+b\bar z\) with \(|a|=|b|=1\); its determinant is zero and its rank is one.
This attains the lower rank bound in (2), and the common field in (1) here is the entire splitting field.
